title: trailboss --json agents new
description: One row: the definition file `agents new` writes, checked as `agents ls` checks one (a name, kind, model, flag or permission it would list with a problem is refused instead). Without --yes nothing is written. It writes only that one file, never over an existing one.

name.description: The definition's name, the file's name without `.json`.

kind.description: claude, codex, gemini, copilot, opencode or pi.

source.description: user (your definitions folder, `~/.config/trailboss/agents/`) or repo (`--repo`: the repository's `.trailboss/agents/`).

path.description: The file it writes, or would write without --yes.

written.description: Whether the file was written: true only with --yes. An existing file is never overwritten (that's an error).

file.description: The file's content, JSON with the fields given (kind, description, model, permission, args, rules), ending in a newline.

trust.description: new for a repository's definition, which starts only once trusted with `agents trust --yes`; null for yours.

command.description: The command it would run, as one line to read, with the brief shown as `<brief>`.

argv.description: The same as separate arguments, run without a shell.
